Lumentum remains confident in an ultra-high-power laser chip demand ramp in the second half of calendar 2027, ahead of customer scale-up deployments in calendar 2028; because the first phase of scale-up optical connections will span across compute racks within the cluster, the ramp applies to any topology larger than one rack. CFO Wajid Ali: ultra-high-power laser revenue is expected 'by the end of the year to be sort of in the $50 million mark', and 'I think the third quarter is when you would see the first triple-digit quarter for ultra-high powered lasers' (fiscal Q3).

items.reason: Restores the CFO's hedge ('sort of', 'I think') on the ultra-high-power laser revenue milestones and attributes them to him.
items.evidence: I think the third quarter is when you would see the first triple-digit quarter for ultra-high powered lasers.

set.signal: Pump lasers: shipments surged more than 80% year-over-year and Lumentum will 'remain effectively sold out for the foreseeable future despite our rapid capacity expansion.' A fourfold increase in pump laser shipments is still expected over the next several quarters. CEO Michael Hurlston: 'rough order, we are somewhere between 70% and 80% share.' Capacity is ramping in Rose Orchard, brought into the Thailand manufacturing for packaging and test. Multiple long-term customer agreements have been secured to help offset planned capital expenditures - formed with, for example, a lot of the NEMs (network equipment manufacturers); for the most part three-year arrangements with pricing built in and pricing levers Lumentum can exercise if certain conditions are met, and 'In most instances, I think they are take or pay.'
